pages.hook: In the USA, people love to show family photos and invite new friends to a family meal. Learn the words to introduce everyone with a smile.

mythfact.s: Americans say “mom” and the British say “mum”.
mythfact.why: It is a classic difference between American and British English.

mythfact.s: Mother’s Day in the USA is in May.
mythfact.why: It is the second Sunday of May, the same as in Brazil.

mythfact.s: Father’s Day is on the same date in the USA and Brazil.
mythfact.why: In the USA it is in June (third Sunday). In Brazil it is in August.

mythfact.s: Minneapolis is known as the “City of Lakes”.
mythfact.why: There are many lakes inside the city of Minneapolis, in Minnesota.

mythfact.s: In English, “family” means only mother, father and children.
mythfact.why: It can include grandparents, cousins, aunts and uncles too.

lines: Hi! Come to dinner on **Sunday** at 6.
Bring your sister. See you soon!

compare.br: In Brazil, large Sunday lunches with grandparents, uncles and cousins are very common.
compare.us: In the USA, family dinners can be smaller, and many families also have a big holiday meal on Thanksgiving.
compare.tip: Say “This is my…” and then the name: “This is my brother, Leo.”
compare.ask: Show a family photo and say who is who in English.

pages.title: Reading quest — My family in Minneapolis · part 1
text: My name is Greta, and I live in Minneapolis, Minnesota. People call my city the “City of Lakes”. Today I want to introduce my **family**.

“**This is my mother** and **my father**,” I tell my new friend Jordan. “**That’s my brother**. **His name is Leo.**” Leo is a student. He plays the guitar. Jordan asks, “**Do you have sisters?**” “**Yes, I have one sister**,” I say. “**She’s a nurse.**” My grandma is also in the photo. She is my best friend.

Jordan smiles. “**Your family is nice!**” “**Thank you!** Do you have a big family?” I ask. “Yes,” says Jordan, “and we always eat together.” Then he says, “**Come to dinner on Sunday!**” I answer, “**I’d love to!**”

fast.why: Greta shows her family to a friend.

tf.why: Leo is a student. The sister is a nurse.

tf.s: Greta says yes to the dinner invitation.

pages.title: Reading quest — My family in Minneapolis · part 2
text: I like to think about a book from 1902. The English writer E. Nesbit wrote “Five Children and It”. Five brothers and sisters find a magic creature in a sand pit. It gives them one wish every day. The children say, “**This is my sister! This is the baby!**” They love each other, but they also argue.
My family is like that book. We are not magic, but we laugh and argue. Family is the place where we learn to say, “This is my…” with love.
